title: Reduced set: packages 1, 3, 7, 8 and every loadable hurdle (12, 13, 16-19, 21, 22, 26-31) with all heads (ev/am25/am50/am75/am80/am85/am90/amstar)
caption: Reduced picker: 1 MSE, 3 weighted xentropy, 7 weighted MSE, 8 pinball 0.30, every loadable hurdle: 12/16 (3-class logloss / ROC-AUC), 13/17 (binary logloss / ROC-AUC), 18/21 (inverted 3-class ROC-AUC / logloss), 19 inverted-binary hurdle ROC-AUC (package 25 was its exact duplicate and was removed), 22 inverted-binary hurdle and the retrained hurdles 26-31 (without user_id/name: 26 logloss, 27 specificity, 28 ROC-AUC with MAE regressor; 29, 30, 31 the same with MSE regressor), each with every head (ev / am25 / am50 / am75 / am80 / am85 / am90 / amstar). amstar tau* maximizes train R2 (min MSE) with native inverted-binary argmax and is frozen (not refit on holdout or live). Live amstar is scored for every hurdle package. Top: last-3-month BNPL production cohort, batches=72. Acceptance n=142,391 (census: every eligible user, no sampling error for this cohort). Delinquency n=2,997 (census: every eligible user, no sampling error for this cohort) (matured CaaS book of the last 180 days). The shaded bands and the "(95% CI)" figures treat each cohort as one draw from ongoing traffic (Wilson interval for the yes-share, delta method for past-due/principal, no finite-population correction). They show how far the rates could move on future traffic, not an error in this cohort's own numbers. Blue = stored autogluon_v25; rust = local AF package 1 MSE; charcoal = selected challenger. Bottom: union Almost Full holdout. Delinquency = 1 − pngi_rate.
note_html:
Top row (production, BNPL only): stored autogluon_v25 from pre_scored_users, the locally scored union Almost Full package 1 MSE on the same users (these two can differ), and the selected challenger. The cohort is every last-3-month BNPL bnpl.api_requests user with a stored v25: a census, not a sample, so the cohort's own rates carry no sampling error. Delinquency = the whole matured BNPL CaaS book of the last 180 days (every user with a matured installment, completed_plans > 0 and a stored v25): also a census.

The shaded bands and the "(95% CI)" figures treat each cohort as one draw from ongoing traffic (Wilson interval for the yes-share, delta method for past-due/principal, no finite-population correction). They show how far the rates could move on future traffic, not an error in this cohort's own numbers.

Bottom row (holdout): gated yes-share of union test_v25.csv (BNPL leftover + cards, same 80/20 split as prior v25). Delinquency = labeled unpaid share 1 − pngi_rate in the score tail — not Fritz CaaS pesos. The original Fritz Pages copy is unchanged.
